title: The heritage trust information line
titleCn: 遗产信托基金会咨询热线

paragraphs.text: Part two.
You will hear a recorded telephone message about a charity which looks after old houses.
First, you have some time to look at questions eleven to seventeen.
Now listen carefully and answer questions eleven to seventeen.

Welcome to the Heritage Trust Information Line. This is a recorded message. You will not be charged for this call. The Heritage Trust is a charity which exists to preserve old properties of national importance. It owns and maintains forty-nine throughout the country, forty-seven of which are open to the public.
The entrance fee varies from property to property, but by becoming a member of the trust, you enjoy many benefits, including free entrance to all its properties.

We offer several different types of membership. The individual membership is our most popular, with an annual cost of twenty-nine pounds fifty. But we also have our senior plan, and that's available for individuals who are fifty-eight years and above and is at the special rate of twenty-one pounds twenty per year.

Obviously, we would not require you to produce proof of age every time you visit a property. But we do ask that when you register for senior membership, you send us a photocopy of your passport. This is all we require for proof of age.
Another type we offer is group membership.

Many school and other educational parties like to take advantage of this special rate, but it can be used for clubs or family groups as you wish. The only requirement is that the group consists of more than twelve people.

The total cost is one hundred and ninety pounds and can be used at any time throughout the week, including weekends. But unfortunately, we are unable to allow visits on national holidays under this plan.
We are very sorry that we have recently had to introduce this condition because crowding can cause damage to our properties, especially on these very popular days.
So how can you become a member?

We offer two different ways to apply for membership. Of course, you can join at any trust property simply by filling in a form in the office. Any one of our staff would be happy to help you do this. And you can also join by post.
Please write to the HT Membership Department, PO Box six five four seven, and that's in Beanam, spelt B-E-A-N-H-A-M, which is in Devonshire, PL23 9PU.
Enclose a check for the relevant amount and send your name, address, and contact telephone number.
Unfortunately, we are not yet able to offer internet joining facilities.

Upon joining, you will receive a welcome pack, which has a wealth of useful information about the trust and its properties. It includes directions to all HT properties. Often, the properties are in very out-of-the-way places, so don't lose the directions.
The pack also gives full information about property opening times, as well as details about any special shows at each site.
Before you hear the rest of the message, you have some time to look at questions eighteen to twenty.
Now listen and answer questions eighteen to twenty.

We are now able to guarantee that all Heritage Trust properties offer the following facilities to visitors: car parking, which is free to all visiting the house. Just keep your entrance ticket or membership card and show it on exit. A special Heritage Trust shop selling a wide range of top-quality merchandise, a restaurant with a particular emphasis on locally produced food, and guided tours in four European languages.
For up-to-date information, each house now has its own website. Just do a search under the name of the house.
We are committed to providing the best
